title: Console performance optimization for Usage Insights (query p95 + end-to-end p95)
creator: Dylan Brooks
body:
Goal
Optimize Usage Insights query latency and end-to-end Console p95 for the route+model breakdown views and “Top cost drivers” panels. This is required for beta usability (customers are using 7d/30d ranges and multi-filter drilldowns; current behavior times out on larger workspaces).

Background / Problem
- Current Insights queries frequently exceed 3–8s for 30-day ranges and can hit gateway timeouts when combined with filters (project+region+route+model) and pagination.
- We saw an incident-style rollback where Insights queries timed out after enabling the initial query path broadly (see incident thread link). Even after rollback, perf is still borderline.
- Customer ticket SUP-24863 indicates 30d range timeouts and confusion about whether data is partial.

Performance targets (beta)
- Query service API p95 latency (server-side):
  - Breakdown table (route+model rollup): <= 900ms p95 for 7d, <= 1500ms p95 for 30d (workspace with ~200 routes, ~25 models, 5M requests/month).
  - Top drivers endpoint: <= 1200ms p95 for 7d, <= 2000ms p95 for 30d.
- End-to-end Console p95 (navigation -> table rendered):
  - 7d: <= 2.5s p95
  - 30d: <= 4.0s p95
- Hard limits:
  - No request should exceed 10s; return a partial-data response only when explicitly supported with banners (ENG-3824), otherwise fail fast with actionable error.

Scope
1) Warehouse query optimization
- Ensure the route_model_agg dataset (ENG-3812) is partitioned by time_bucket (daily/hourly) and clustered by (workspace_id, project_id, route_norm, model_family, model_version_bucket).
- Add/verify indexes/materialized views for the most common query shapes:
  - workspace_id + time_bucket + project_id
  - workspace_id + time_bucket + route_norm
  - workspace_id + time_bucket + model_version_bucket
- Reduce expensive DISTINCT / high-cardinality group-bys:
  - Prefer pre-aggregated metrics for token_in/token_out, cache_hit/miss, retry_count, fallback_count.
  - Move context_length_distribution buckets into a fixed histogram representation (e.g., <=1k, 1–2k, 2–4k, 4–8k, 8k+), aggregated upstream.

2) Pre-aggregation strategy
- Confirm aggregation granularity:
  - Default for UI: daily buckets for >7d, hourly buckets for <=7d.
  - Route+model table is computed from pre-aggregated buckets; query service should not read raw request events.
- Add a “top N routes per workspace per day” helper table to speed “Top cost drivers” when customers have many routes (guardrails still apply in ENG-3818).

3) Caching
- Add a query service response cache keyed by:
  - workspace_id, project_id, env, region, time_range, time_zone, route_norm, model_bucket, pagination params
- TTL policy:
  - Default TTL 60s for <=24h ranges, 5m for >24h ranges.
  - Cache must incorporate data freshness watermark; invalidate when watermark changes (tie into freshness metadata work).
- Add ETag/If-None-Match for identical queries from console back/forward navigation.

4) Query simplifications / API guardrails (perf-driven)
- Enforce a maximum time range for interactive UI queries (initial): 31 days. (Longer ranges require export flow.)
- Limit the number of filter combinations and grouping dimensions:
  - For interactive: at most two breakdown dimensions at a time (route+model is the primary); others as filters.
- Pagination strategy:
  - Use stable ordering (total_cost desc, then route_norm, model_bucket) to prevent expensive offset scans.
  - Prefer cursor-based pagination for large result sets (coordinate with ENG-3814 contract if not already).

5) Console performance
- Reduce re-fetch loops in the table page:
  - De-dupe requests across components; fetch breakdown + freshness + top drivers in a single fanout with shared time range state.
- Ensure loading state does not block rendering of filters and prior cached results.

Deliverables
- A perf test plan (automated + manual) covering representative workspaces and query patterns.
- Profiling notes and “before/after” metrics dashboards.
- PRs for warehouse changes (partition/cluster/index/materialized view), query service caching, and any API pagination changes required.
- Updated guidance for support: recommended time ranges and how to diagnose timeouts (ties to known issues).

Perf test plan
Datasets / scenarios
- Synthetic dataset generator (or replay) for:
  - Small: 10 routes, 5 models, 200k requests/month
  - Medium: 200 routes, 25 models, 5M requests/month
  - Large: 2k routes (post-normalization), 50 models, 25M requests/month
- Mix includes:
  - 20% streaming
  - 5% retries
  - 2% fallbacks
  - Cache hit rates: 0%, 30%, 70% (to validate cache metrics path)

Load tests
- k6/locust style load against query service:
  - 30 RPS sustained for 15 min on breakdown endpoint
  - 10 RPS sustained for 15 min on top drivers
  - Burst: 100 RPS for 60s to simulate release/beta account onboarding
- Measure:
  - p50/p95/p99 latency
  - error rate by status (429/5xx/timeouts)
  - warehouse query time distribution and total scanned bytes

UI tests
- Playwright flow to simulate:
  - open Insights page -> change time range 1d/7d/30d -> apply filter -> drilldown -> back
  - ensure <1 duplicate request per user action (network assertions)

Acceptance criteria
- Meets beta latency targets above on Medium dataset, and does not exceed 10s even on Large dataset (must degrade gracefully with actionable error and “try export” guidance).
- No regression in correctness (totals match billing reconciliation tolerance); query optimizations must not change attribution semantics.
- Cache correctness validated: same query returns identical totals across cache hits; watermark invalidation works.

Open questions
- Cursor-based pagination: do we need to change API contract now or can we implement in query service behind the same response shape? (Action: Felix to confirm what’s already in ENG-3814)
- Materialized views ownership: Telemetry team (Logan/Mei) vs Platform Eng (Thomas). (Proposal: Telemetry owns tables/views; query service only reads.)

Risks / Mitigations
- Risk: Optimizing by adding views increases warehouse cost.
  - Mitigation: track cost per query in benchmarks doc; add alerts for scanned bytes/query; cap interactive range to 31d.
- Risk: Cache hides freshness delays.
  - Mitigation: always return freshness watermark in response and render banner when lagging; cache key includes watermark.

Work breakdown
- [ ] Baseline measurements on current beta account + synthetic Medium dataset
- [ ] Implement clustering/index/materialized view changes for primary query
- [ ] Add response caching + ETag support
- [ ] Optimize pagination path (cursor or stable limited scan)
- [ ] Console request de-dupe + avoid waterfall fetches
- [ ] Run perf test plan, publish results, and update SLO doc if needed

Updates / Comments
2026-02-03 (Thomas Baird)
- Reproduced 30d timeout on Medium dataset when filtering by project+region; warehouse query plan shows full scan on route_norm due to missing clustering on route_norm + model_bucket. Proposed adding clustering and a lightweight MV for (workspace_id, day, route_norm, model_bucket).

2026-02-08 (Mei Lin)
- Added draft MV definition in the warehouse repo; waiting on confirmation from Nadia that it won’t break attribution edge cases around retries/fallbacks (specifically, whether retries are counted on final route/model or original).

2026-02-14 (Felix Schneider)
- Query service caching prototype shows ~65% hit rate during normal console navigation (filter toggles still bust cache). Need to normalize filter params ordering and ensure time_zone is consistent.

2026-02-20 (Dylan Brooks)
- This remains a beta blocker. We should not expand allowlist until Medium dataset p95 is under 1.5s for 30d and the console no longer hits timeouts. Also please coordinate with ENG-3824 so that any partial/lagging data is clearly surfaced to avoid support churn.
